title: Alternative air–liquid interface method for inhalation toxicity testing of a petroleum-derived substance
author: Sandra, An, et al.
materials: For the measurement of total gasoline and BTEX (benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and (p + m)-xylene, o-xylene) the samples (cells and/or CCM dispersed in blank water) were doped with the isotope-labelled compound D10-EB by injection through the membrane in the lid of the sealed vial. The HS sampler heats the vial at 70 °C for 30 min. During this period the gasoline transitions from the sample matrix into the vapor phase above. A fixed volume of the headspace vapor is extracted from the vial and injected into a capillary column for GC separation. A MS is used to detect and quantify the gasoline or BTEX (Thermo HS-GC–MS).

steps.title: Sample desiccator headspace
steps.instruction: After 1 h exposure, draw air at 10 mL min⁻¹ for 10 min through a coconut‑activated charcoal sorbent tube (SKC 226‑09) placed in the desiccator headspace, keeping a HEPA‑filtered inlet open to prevent vacuum.

steps.title: Extract sorbent tubes
steps.instruction: Remove the charcoal tubes and extract the adsorbed compounds with carbon disulfide containing the internal standard 2‑fluorotoluene; collect the extract for GC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Perform GC‑MS analysis of extract
steps.instruction: Inject the extract into an Agilent 6890 N GC coupled to an Agilent 5975 MS using a non‑polar Rtx‑502.2 column (30 m × 0.25 mm, df 1.4 µm) with helium as carrier gas; quantify gasoline by linear regression against the internal standard and calculate air concentration from the extracted amount, sampling rate, and sampling time.

steps.title: Prepare cell and medium samples
steps.instruction: Immediately after exposure, add 100 µL culture medium to the apical side of the A549 insert, scrape the cells, and transfer the cell‑containing medium into a 20 mL glass vial containing 4.5 mL blank water; also cut the membrane and place it in a similar vial with 4.5 mL blank water; finally collect 600 µL cell‑culture medium (CCM) from each condition into a glass vial with 4.5 mL blank water. Seal all vials airtight with aluminum caps.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL medium to apical side and scrape cells.
Transfer the 100 µL cell‑containing medium to a 20 mL glass vial with 4.5 mL blank water and seal.
Cut the membrane, place it in a similar vial with 4.5 mL blank water and seal.
Collect 600 µL CCM from each condition into a glass vial with 4.5 mL blank water and seal.

steps.title: Add isotope label and heat
steps.instruction: Inject the isotope‑labelled compound D10‑EB into each sealed vial through the lid membrane, then place the vials in a headspace sampler set to 70 °C for 30 min to equilibrate gasoline into the vapor phase; extract a fixed volume of headspace vapor for injection into the GC.

steps.title: Measure total gasoline by scan mode
steps.instruction: Run the GC‑MS in scan mode (m/z 30‑250) and quantify total gasoline using the internal‑standard method based on the integrated peak area of the total ion current chromatogram (retention time 3‑30 min) and the characteristic ion of D10‑EB; use a calibration standard of gasoline with internal standard to determine response factors.

steps.title: Measure BTEX by SIM mode
steps.instruction: Switch the GC‑MS to selective ion monitoring (SIM) targeting BTEX ions; quantify each BTEX component using the internal‑standard method with calibration standards of benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, (p + m)-xylene, o‑xylene and D10‑EB to calculate concentrations.
